newsitem.title: USA: China to get $50 mln US EXIM Bank loan for energy.
newsitem.headline: China to get $50 mln US EXIM Bank loan for energy.

text.p: China will get a $50 million credit line from the U.S. Export-Import Bank to help finance a number of modest projects involving renewable energy and efficiency, U.S. Energy Department officials said Thursday.

After meetings this week between U.S. and Chinese energy officials, the countries also decided to hold an oil and natural gas forum early next year to consider ways U.S. energy companies can increase their role in China, the officials said in a telephone briefing.
Energy Secretary Federico Pena met here Wednesday and Thursday with the Chinese Vice Chairman of the State Planning Commission Ye Qing on bilaterial energy cooperation.

The department officials said they discussed a broad range of issues that also included nuclear technology, clean coal technology, China's need for increased foreign investment in its energy sector, and environmental issues including global warming.

The $50 million EXIM bank loan is the first in partnership with the Energy Department and would be for "smaller projects that often go under the radar screen" of the bank, an Energy Department official said.
It is to finance projects in the $5-$10 million range such as photovoltaics, wind, or biomass energy, and small co-generation projects, they said.
If there is sufficient demand for projects, the credit line could be extended, they said.
On the proposed oil and gas conference, a department official said the purpose will be "to explore new ways" for U.S. companies to be involved in China's energy sector.
"We're hoping for the broadest participation," the official said, adding he expected virtually all U.S. oil and companies will be interested.
